p.src: After Third Sister You had taken her own life, her mother, Second Sister You, Jia Zhen, Jia Lian, and the others were naturally overwhelmed with grief. They hurriedly had her laid out with full ceremony and taken beyond the city for burial. When Liu Xianglian saw that Third Sister You was dead, he was lost in grief and longing; but a few cold words from the Taoist shattered the delusion that bound him. He cut off his hair, renounced the world, and drifted away with the mad Taoist, none knew whither. But we shall leave them for the present.

p.src: Now, Aunt Xue had been delighted to learn that Xianglian had become formally betrothed to Third Sister You. She was happily planning to buy him a house, furnish his household, and choose an auspicious day for the wedding, thereby repaying him for saving her son's life. Suddenly some young servants in the household began clamoring that “Third Sister has killed herself.” The little maids overheard them and reported it to Aunt Xue. Aunt Xue did not know why she had done it and sighed deeply. While she was still puzzling over it, Baochai came in from the garden. Aunt Xue said to her, “My child, have you heard? Third Sister, the younger sister of your sister-in-law Zhen, had already been promised to Liu Xianglian, your brother's sworn brother, had she not? Yet for some unknown reason she has cut her own throat. And no one knows where Liu Xianglian has gone either. It is truly an extraordinary affair—quite beyond anyone's imagining.” Baochai heard this without appearing greatly concerned and replied, “The proverb puts it well: ‘The sky may bring unforeseen storms, and people may meet fortune or calamity overnight.’ This too was ordained for them in a former life. The other day, because he had saved Brother's life, you were discussing how to make arrangements for him. Now one is dead and the other gone, so in my opinion we can only leave matters as they are. You need not grieve over them either. What matters more is that it has been ten or twenty days since Brother returned from the South. By now the goods he brought back should all have been distributed. The assistants who accompanied him worked very hard and have been home for several months already. You ought to discuss it with Brother and invite them to a feast as a token of thanks. Otherwise people may think us discourteous.”

p.src: While mother and daughter were still talking, Xue Pan came in from outside, the traces of tears still visible in his eyes. As soon as he entered, he clapped his hands and said to his mother, “Mother, have you heard what happened to Second Brother Liu and Third Sister You?” Aunt Xue replied, “I have only just heard. I was discussing the whole affair with your sister here.” Xue Pan asked, “Have you also heard that Liu Xianglian renounced the world and went off with a Taoist?” “That makes it stranger still,” said Aunt Xue. “How could a clever young man like Master Liu lose his head for a moment and go off with a Taoist? You and he were good friends, and he has neither parents nor brothers, but is all alone here. You should search everywhere for him. How far could he have gone with that Taoist? Surely he can only be in some nearby Taoist or Buddhist temple.” “Of course,” said Xue Pan. “The moment I heard the news, I hurried out with the young servants and searched everywhere, but found not so much as his shadow. I asked people too, but they all said they had not seen him.” Aunt Xue said, “Since you have searched for him without finding him, you have done all that friendship requires of you. Who can say that he has not gained some benefit by renouncing the world? But now you should also attend to your business and make early preparations for everything needed for your own marriage. We have few people in our household, and as the saying goes, ‘The clumsy bird must take wing first.’ Make sure everything is ready, lest at the last moment things be forgotten or found wanting and people laugh at us. Besides, as your sister just said, you have been home for more than half a month, so the goods ought to have been distributed by now. You should give a banquet for the assistants who went with you and let them recover from their labors. They traveled two or three thousand li at your side, endured four or five months of hardship, and on the road bore so many frights and heavy burdens on your behalf.” Having heard her out, Xue Pan said, “You are quite right, Mother. Sister has thought of everything. I had been thinking the same thing, but these past few days the commotion of distributing the goods everywhere has left my head in a whirl. Then I spent several days rushing about on Second Brother Liu's account, only to have it all come to nothing. I made a great fuss to no purpose and let the proper business fall behind. If there is no objection, I shall fix the date for tomorrow or the day after and send out the invitations.” “See to it as you think best,” said Aunt Xue.

p.src: Before he had finished speaking, a young servant came in from outside and reported, “Steward Zhang has sent someone with two chests of things. He says these were purchased separately by you, Master, and were not entered in the merchandise account. They were meant to be delivered sooner, but they were buried beneath the merchandise chests and could not be taken out. The goods were all dispatched yesterday, so they have only been delivered today.” As he spoke, two more young servants were seen carrying in two large brown chests reinforced with wooden boards. At the sight of them, Xue Pan exclaimed, “Good heavens! How could I have grown so muddleheaded? I brought these especially for Mother and my sister, yet I completely forgot to have them brought home. It took one of the clerks to send them over.” Baochai said, “Listen to you! These things you brought ‘especially’ have already lain there for ten or twenty days. Had you not brought them especially, I suppose they would not have arrived until the end of the year. You really are far too careless about everything.” Xue Pan laughed. “I suppose someone frightened the soul out of me on the journey, and it has not yet found its way back into my body.” They all laughed for a while, then told a little maid, “Go out and tell the servants that the things have been received and they may go back.” Aunt Xue and Baochai asked, “What can possibly be inside, to have been bound up so securely?” Xue Pan ordered the two young servants to come in. They untied the ropes, removed the boards, and opened the lock. The first chest proved to contain silks, satins, brocades, imported goods, and other articles for everyday use. Xue Pan said with a smile, “The other chest is what I brought for my sister.” He went over and opened it himself. When mother and daughter examined it, they found brushes, ink, paper, inkstones, writing paper in many colors, scented sachets, fragrant beads, fans, fan pendants, face powder, rouge, and other such things. There were also novelties brought from Tiger Hill: mechanical figures that moved by themselves, drinking-game pieces, little mercury-filled tumblers that turned somersaults, sand lanterns, and sets of clay figures depicting scenes from plays, each set housed in a box covered with blue gauze. There was also a clay statuette of Xue Pan modeled at Tiger Hill, which resembled him exactly. Baochai paid no attention to the other things. She picked up the statuette of Xue Pan and studied it carefully, then looked at her brother, and could not help laughing. She then told Ying’er to have several older maids carry the things, chest and all, to the Garden. After chatting a while longer with her mother and brother, she returned to the Garden herself. Meanwhile, Aunt Xue took the contents from the other chest, sorted them carefully into separate portions, and had Tongxi deliver them to Grandmother Jia, Lady Wang, and the others. No more need be said of this.

p.src: The young ladies all received their gifts, rewarded the messengers, and said they would offer their thanks in person when next they met Baochai. Lin Daiyu alone, on seeing articles from her native region, was moved by them to sorrow. She remembered that both her parents were dead, that she had neither brother nor sister, and that she was living as a dependent in a relative’s household. Who was there to bring local gifts for me? she thought. At this thought, grief overcame her once more. Zijuan understood Daiyu’s feelings perfectly, but did not dare speak of them openly. She merely tried to comfort her from the side: “Miss, you have always been frail and must take medicine morning and evening. These last two days you have seemed a little better than before. Though your spirits have improved somewhat, you are by no means fully recovered. The things Miss Bao sent today show how highly she has always regarded you. You ought to be pleased when you see them, so why have they made you sad instead? Surely you would not have it seem that Miss Bao’s gifts have only caused you distress? If Miss Bao were to hear of it, she would feel embarrassed as well. Besides, the Old Lady and the others here, concerned about your health, have gone to every possible trouble to find good physicians to examine you and prescribe medicines, all so that you might recover. Now that you have only just begun to improve, if you weep and grieve like this again, are you not harming your own health and adding to the Old Lady’s worries when she sees you? What is more, your illness arose in the first place because constant worry damaged your blood and vital energies. Your precious health is not something you should make light of yourself.” While Zijuan was still consoling her, they heard a little maid call from the courtyard, “Second Master Bao is here.” Zijuan quickly said, “Please ask Second Master to come in.”

p.src: Just then Baoyu came into the room. After Daiyu had invited him to sit down, he saw her face streaked with tears and asked, “Little sister, who has upset you this time?” Daiyu forced a smile. “Who says I am upset?” Beside her, Zijuan pursed her lips toward the table behind the bed. Baoyu understood and looked over. Seeing a great heap of things, he knew that Baochai had sent them and teased, “What are all these things doing here? Surely you aren’t planning to open a general store?” Daiyu made no reply. Zijuan laughed. “Second Master, you had better not mention those things. Miss Bao sent some things over, and the moment our young lady saw them, she grew heartsick. I was just trying to console her. You have arrived at the perfect moment, Second Master; please help us cheer her up.” Baoyu knew perfectly well why Daiyu was distressed, but dared not broach the subject. He could only say with a smile, “I imagine your young lady is troubled for no other reason than that Miss Bao sent too few things, and so she is angry and sad. Don’t worry, little sister. Next year I shall send someone south of the Yangzi to bring you back two whole boatloads, so that you needn’t keep wiping away tears.” Hearing this, Daiyu knew that Baoyu was trying to amuse her. Neither wishing to rebuff him nor to indulge him, she said, “However little I may know of the world, I have not sunk so low as to become angry and heartbroken merely because too few gifts were sent. I am not a child of two or three. You think me far too petty-minded. I have my own reasons, though you know nothing of them.” As she spoke, tears began to flow again. Baoyu hurried to the bed and sat close beside Daiyu. Picking up the gifts one by one and turning them over for a careful look, he deliberately asked what each was, what it was called, what another was made of to be so finely fashioned, and what yet another was and how it was used. He said that one piece could be displayed close at hand, and that another would look splendid as an antique on the long side table. He kept muddling along with this stream of inconsequential chatter. Seeing Baoyu behave like this, Daiyu began to feel sorry for him and said, “You needn’t keep making a muddle of things here. Let us go over to Sister Bao’s.” Baoyu desired nothing more than for Daiyu to go out, dispel her gloom, and ease her grief, so he replied, “Since Sister Bao has sent us gifts, we ought indeed to go and thank her.” Daiyu said, “There is no need for that between sisters. But now that Brother Xue has returned, he will surely tell her about some of the historic sites in the south. I should like to listen; it will be almost as if I had made a journey home.” As she spoke, her eyes reddened once more. Baoyu stood and waited for her. Daiyu had no choice but to come out with him, and together they went to Baochai’s quarters.

p.src: Meanwhile, after hearing what his mother had said, Xue Pan hastily sent out invitations and prepared a banquet. The next day, the four business associates he had invited all arrived, and naturally they discussed sales, accounts, and the dispatch of goods. Before long they took their places at table, and Xue Pan poured wine for each of them in turn. Aunt Xue also sent someone out to convey her regards. They drank and chatted idly. One of them asked Xue Pan, “Why didn’t you invite Second Master Liu?” At this, Xue Pan knitted his brows, sighed, and said, “Don’t even mention Second Master Liu. It is the strangest thing under heaven. Second Master Liu indeed! By now, who knows where he has gone to become Taoist Master Liu?” Everyone exclaimed in astonishment, “What do you mean?” Xue Pan then related the whole story of what had happened to Xianglian. They were even more horrified when they heard it and said, “No wonder the other day at the shop we seemed to hear people clamoring that a Taoist had converted a man with just a few words and taken him away, while others said a gust of wind had swept him off. We simply did not know who it was. We were busy dispatching goods and had no leisure to inquire into the matter, so even now we scarcely knew whether to believe it. Who would have thought it was Second Master Liu? Had we known it was he, all of us ought to have tried to dissuade him. Whatever happened, we would never have let him go.” One of them said, “Perhaps it happened this way?” When the others asked what he meant, the man replied, “Someone as clever as Second Master Liu may not truly have gone off as the Taoist’s disciple. He knows some martial arts and is strong besides. Perhaps he saw through the Taoist’s sorcery and wicked tricks and deliberately followed him in order to deal with him in secret. That is also possible.” Xue Pan said, “If that is truly so, then all may yet be well. Why is there no one to punish those who spread heresies and delude the public?” The others asked, “Once you learned of it, surely you went looking for him?” Xue Pan said, “Where inside or outside the city did I not search? You may laugh at me, but when I could not find him, I even wept.” After saying this, he did nothing but heave long and short sighs, listless and dispirited, quite unlike his usual cheerful self. Seeing him in this state, his business associates naturally felt it improper to remain long. They merely drank a few cups of wine, ate their meal, and then all departed.

p.src: Meanwhile, Baoyu accompanied Daiyu to Baochai’s quarters. When Baoyu saw Baochai, he said, “Your elder brother went to such trouble to bring these things back. You should have kept them for yourself instead of giving them to us.” Baochai smiled. “They are nothing particularly fine—merely some local products brought from far away. Their novelty is all that makes them interesting.” Daiyu said, “We paid no attention to such things when we were children, but now that I see them again, they truly do seem rare and novel.” Baochai smiled and said, “As you know, little sister, this is just what the saying means: ‘Things gain value far from home.’ What are they really worth, after all?” These words touched directly upon what had just been troubling Daiyu, so Baoyu hastily changed the subject. “When elder brother goes there again next year, he must be sure to bring us more.” Daiyu shot him a glance. “If you want them, say so yourself. There is no need to drag anyone else into it. Look, sister—Brother Bao has not come to thank you at all; he has actually come to place his order for next year!” At this, both Baochai and Baoyu laughed. The three chatted idly for a while longer, until the subject turned to Daiyu’s illness. After offering her some advice, Baochai said, “If you feel unwell, little sister, you should make yourself get up and walk about a little to take your mind off things. That is better, after all, than sitting shut up in your room feeling stifled. Those other two days, did I not feel listless and feverish all over, wanting only to lie down? p.src: She had just reached the bank by Qinfang Bridge. It was late summer and early autumn; in the pond, fresh and withered lotuses mingled, their red and green leaves spreading in profusion. As Xiren walked, she lingered awhile along the embankment, admiring the view. Suddenly looking up, she saw someone beneath the grape arbor wielding a duster at something. When she drew near, she found it was old Mother Zhu. Seeing Xiren, the old woman came forward with a broad smile and said, “How is it you have found time for a stroll today, miss?” “Indeed,” replied Xiren. “I am on my way to see Second Mistress Lian. What are you doing here?” “I’m driving the bees away,” said the old woman. “There was little rain during the hottest days this year, so all these fruit trees are infested with insects. They have pitted and scarred the fruit, and a great many have fallen. You may not know it, miss, but hornets are the worst. They need only bite through two or three grapes in a bunch; the juice from the damaged ones drips onto the sound ones, and the whole bunch rots. Just look, miss—in the brief time we have been talking instead of chasing them, ever so many have settled there already.” “Even if you chased them without pause, you could never drive so many away,” said Xiren. “You would do better to tell the purchasing steward to have plenty of little bags made from thin gauze and slip one over each bunch. They would let in air and keep the fruit from being spoiled.” “You are quite right, miss,” the old woman said with a smile. “This is my first year in charge of them; how could I have known such a clever method?” Then she added with another smile, “Though the fruit has suffered somewhat this year, it tastes very good. If you do not believe me, let me pick one for you to try.” Xiren grew serious. “How could that be permitted? Not only is the fruit still unripe and unfit to eat, but even if it were ripe, none has yet been offered to our superiors. How could we eat it first? You have served in this household for years. Surely you have not forgotten even this rule?” Old Mother Zhu hastily smiled. “You are right, miss. “I only dared suggest it because I saw how much you liked them, but in doing so I broke the rules. I truly am a muddleheaded old woman.” “It is nothing serious,” said Xiren. “Only you older women should take care not to be the first to set such an example.” With that, she went straight out through the garden gate and made her way to Xifeng’s quarters.

p.src: As soon as she entered the courtyard, she heard Xifeng exclaim, “Heaven is my witness! After all I have endured in this house, I am being treated more and more like a thief!” Hearing this, Xiren knew something was amiss. Yet she could neither turn back nor enter unannounced, so she deliberately made her footsteps heavier and called through the window, “Sister Ping, are you at home?” Ping’er promptly answered and came out to welcome her. Xiren asked, “Is Second Mistress at home too? Is she quite recovered?” By the time she finished speaking, she had already entered the room. Xifeng had been pretending to recline on the bed. When she saw Xiren enter, she smiled and sat up, saying, “I am better, thank you for thinking of me. Why have you not come to sit with us these past few days?” “Since you were unwell, madam, I ought by rights to have come every day to inquire after you,” said Xiren. “But I feared that, feeling poorly, you would need peace and quiet to rest, and that our coming might only disturb and weary you.” Xifeng smiled. “You could never be a bother. But though there are many people in Brother Bao’s rooms, he relies on you alone to look after him, so you truly cannot get away. Ping’er often tells me that you still think of me when I am not there and frequently ask after my health. That shows how conscientious you are.” As she spoke, she told Ping’er to move a low stool beside the bed and invited Xiren to sit down. Feng’er brought in tea, and Xiren half rose courteously, saying, “Please sit down, little sister.” They continued chatting of this and that. Presently, a young maid could be seen whispering to Ping’er in the outer room, “Wang’er is here. He is waiting at the inner gate.” Then Xiren heard Ping’er whisper back, “Very well. Tell him to go away for now and come back later. He must not stand waiting at the gate.” Realizing they had business to attend to, Xiren exchanged another few words with Xifeng, then rose to leave. “Come and sit with me whenever you are free,” said Xifeng. “Talking with you cheers me up.” Then she instructed Ping’er, “See your sister out.” Ping’er assented and accompanied Xiren outside. There Xiren saw two or three young maids all standing in attendance, silent and scarcely daring to breathe. Not knowing what the matter was, Xiren went on her way.

p.src: After seeing Xiren out, Ping'er came back and reported, “Wang'er arrived just now. Since Xiren was here, I told him to wait outside for a while. Shall I summon him at once now, or let him wait? Please tell me what you wish done.” “Send him in,” said Xifeng. Ping'er promptly sent a young maid to fetch Wang'er. Meanwhile, Xifeng asked Ping'er again, “Just how did you come to hear about it?” “It was what that young maid said earlier,” replied Ping'er. She said that while she was inside the second gate, she overheard two pages outside saying, ‘This new Second Mistress is even prettier than our old Second Mistress, and she has a better temper too.’ Then someone—Wang'er, she thought, though she was not sure—gave the pair a fierce scolding: ‘What is this nonsense about new mistresses and old mistresses? Be quiet at once! If the people inside hear you, they will cut out your tongues!’” As Ping'er was speaking, a young maid came in and announced, “Wang'er is waiting outside, ready to attend you.” Xifeng gave a cold laugh when she heard this. “Send him in.” The young maid went out and said, “Mistress wants you.” Wang'er hastily acknowledged the summons and entered. After paying his respects, Wang'er stood respectfully with lowered hands at the doorway of the outer room. “Come closer,” said Xifeng. “I have something to ask you.” Only then did Wang'er step over and stand beside the doorway of the inner room. Xifeng asked, “Your Second Master has taken up with a woman outside. Did you know about it or not?” Wang'er knelt in formal obeisance again and replied, “This servant is on duty at the second gate every day. How could I know anything about Second Master's affairs outside?” Xifeng sneered. “Naturally you know nothing. For if you knew, why would you try to stop people from talking?” At this, Wang'er realized that word of what had just happened had already leaked out and that concealment was impossible. Kneeling again, he replied, “I truly know nothing about it. It was only that Xing'er and Xi'er were talking nonsense there earlier, so I rebuked them a couple of times. I do not know the truth or the details, and I dare not make a reckless report. Please question Xing'er, Mistress. He regularly accompanies Second Master when he goes out.” Xifeng spat violently and cursed, “You whole pack of heartless, muddleheaded little bastards! You are all strung together on the same vine, and you imagine I know nothing. Go and fetch that little bastard Xing'er at once—and you are not to leave either. Once I have questioned him thoroughly, I shall come back to you. Fine, fine, fine! What an excellent servant I have trained!” Wang'er had no choice but to answer “Yes” several times in succession. He knocked his head on the floor, scrambled to his feet, and went out to summon Xing'er.

p.src: Now Xing'er was amusing himself with the pages in the accounts office. When he heard that the Second Mistress had summoned him, he started in fright, though it never occurred to him that this particular affair had come to light. He hastily followed Wang'er inside. Wang'er went in first and reported, “Xing'er is here.” “Send him in!” Xifeng ordered harshly. At the sound of her voice, Xing'er lost all presence of mind. He had no choice but to muster his courage and enter. The moment Xifeng saw him, she said, “Well done, you young rascal! What a fine deed you and your master have accomplished! Now tell me the truth!” Hearing this and seeing Xifeng's expression and the looks of the maids on either side, Xing'er went limp with terror. He sank to his knees and did nothing but kowtow. Xifeng said, “As far as the affair itself is concerned, I have heard that you had no hand in it. But your failure to report it to me sooner was your fault. If you tell me the truth, I may still spare you. But if even one word is false, first feel your shoulders and count how many heads you have!” Trembling, Xing'er kowtowed toward her and said, “What affair is Mistress asking about? What have Master and I done wrong?” At this, all the fury pent up inside Xifeng erupted. “Slap his mouth!” she shouted. Wang'er stepped forward and was just about to strike him when Xifeng cursed, “You muddleheaded little bastard! I told him to slap himself. Who asked you to do it? It will not be too late for each of you to slap your own mouth in a moment.” Xing'er obediently struck himself more than a dozen times, first with one hand and then the other. “Stop!” shouted Xifeng. Then she asked, “I suppose you know nothing about your Second Master taking some so-called new mistress or old mistress outside?” When Xing'er heard her name the affair, he grew more frantic than ever. Snatching off his cap, he knocked his head against the brick floor with resounding thuds and cried, “I beg Mistress to spare my miserable life! I shall not dare utter a single word of falsehood.” “Speak at once!” ordered Xifeng. Xing'er straightened up on his knees and reported, “At first, I knew nothing about this affair either. It happened on the day when the Elder Master of the Eastern Mansion escorted the funeral procession and Yu Lu went to Master Zhen's temple to collect some money. Second Master went to the Eastern Mansion with young Master Rong, and on the way the two of them began talking about the two younger sisters staying with Mistress Zhen. Second Master praised her beauty, and young Master Rong egged him on, saying he would arrange for Second Sister to become Second Master's wife.” Hearing this, Xifeng spat vehemently. “Pah! You shameless bastard! Since when was she any sister-in-law of yours?” Xing'er hastily kowtowed again. “This servant deserves death!” He looked up at her but did not dare say another word. “Is that the end of it?” asked Xifeng. Why have you stopped talking?”

Trembling, Xing'er kowtowed toward her and said, “What affair is Mistress asking about? What have Master and I done wrong?”
At this, all the fury pent up inside Xifeng erupted. “Slap his mouth!” she shouted.
Wang'er stepped forward and was just about to strike him when Xifeng cursed, “You muddleheaded little bastard!
I told him to slap himself. Who asked you to do it?
It will not be too late for each of you to slap your own mouth in a moment.”
Xing'er obediently struck himself more than a dozen times, first with one hand and then the other.
“Stop!” shouted Xifeng. Then she asked, “I suppose you know nothing about your Second Master taking some so-called new mistress or old mistress outside?”

When Xing'er heard her name the affair, he grew more frantic than ever. Snatching off his cap, he knocked his head against the brick floor with resounding thuds and cried, “I beg Mistress to spare my miserable life! I shall not dare utter a single word of falsehood.”
“Speak at once!” ordered Xifeng.
Xing'er straightened up on his knees and reported, “At first, I knew nothing about this affair either.
It happened on the day when the Elder Master of the Eastern Mansion escorted the funeral procession and Yu Lu went to Master Zhen's temple to collect some money.
Second Master went to the Eastern Mansion with young Master Rong, and on the way the two of them began talking about the two younger sisters staying with Mistress Zhen.
Second Master praised her beauty, and young Master Rong egged him on, saying he would arrange for Second Sister to become Second Master's wife.”
Hearing this, Xifeng spat vehemently. “Pah! You shameless bastard!
Since when was she any sister-in-law of yours?”
Xing'er hastily kowtowed again. “This servant deserves death!”
He looked up at her but did not dare say another word.
“Is that the end of it?” asked Xifeng.
Why have you stopped talking?”

p.src: Xifeng asked again, “During those days when you said you were attending to business at the other mansion, I suppose this was the business you meant.” Xing'er replied, “Sometimes I did attend to business, and sometimes I went to the new house.” Xifeng asked, “Who lives with her?” Xing'er said, “Her mother and her younger sister. Yesterday her sister cut her own throat.” “Why was that?” asked Xifeng. Xing'er then related the whole affair concerning Liu Xianglian. Xifeng said, “That man was fortunate after all; he escaped becoming a notorious cuckold.” Then she asked, “Is there nothing else?” Xing'er said, “I know nothing of any other matters. Every word I have just spoken is true. If you discover even one false word, madam, you may beat me to death, and I shall bear no resentment.” Xifeng lowered her head for a while, then pointed at Xing'er and said, “You little monkey deserve to be beaten to death. Why should any of this have been hidden from me? You thought that by keeping it from me, you could curry favor with that muddle-headed master of yours and have your new mistress dote on you. If I had not seen that you were still somewhat afraid just now and did not dare lie, I would have had your legs smashed!” With that, she barked, “Get up.” Xing'er kowtowed, then scrambled to his feet and retreated to the doorway of the outer room, not daring to leave at once. Xifeng said, “Come back. I have more to say.” Xing'er hurried back and stood with hands lowered, listening respectfully. Xifeng said, “Why are you in such a hurry? Is your new mistress waiting to reward you with something?” Xing'er did not even dare raise his head. Xifeng said, “From today onward, you are not permitted to go there. Whenever I summon you, you are to appear at once. Just try being even a moment late! Now get out.” Xing'er hastily answered “Yes” several times and withdrew through the door. Xifeng called again, “Xing'er!” Xing'er immediately answered and returned. Xifeng said, “You are going straight out to tell your Second Master, are you not?” Xing'er replied, “I would not dare.” Xifeng said, “If you breathe a single word outside, look out for your hide!” Only after Xing'er had hurriedly promised obedience did he leave. Xifeng then called, “Where is Wang'er?” Wang'er promptly answered and came forward. Xifeng stared fixedly at him for as long as it would take to exchange two or three remarks before saying, “Very good, Wang'er. Very good indeed. You may go! If anyone outside breathes a word of this, I shall hold you responsible for it all.” Wang'er assented and went out as well.
